english: In that year it did not rain. The well dried up. Grief seized the man's heart. The heat burned the field, and the cattle were thirsty. He lifted his own hands and said: "Father Sky, where is the water? Give us rain!" Then Sky heard him. Thunder arrived, and the rain-cloud rose. It rained. The cattle ran to the well, and drank. He became joyful.

english: When night arrives, the cattle come. Standing in the enclosure, the cheerful woman milks them. Her daughter milks the sheep. They give much. She says: "Stand, cattle!" They are standing. The man sits. No one comes. They lie down. They are sated.

english: Dawn became bright. The shepherd led the cattle out of the cow-stall. The swift he-goat went ahead. The sheep and the horse followed. They came to the pasture. They ate. He sat down and watched them. Then he drove them to the well, and they drank. They became sated. When night arrived, he drove them on to the enclosure.

pie: gʷówes dukté. h₂érh₃trom dukté. yugóm bʰérete. lóyseh₂m h₃roǵéyete. mē h₃slidʰté. gʷʰrensós dʰégʷʰeti swidyómes-kʷe. h₂nḗr wos sékʷetor. séh₁mn̥ séh₁yoh₂. dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr dʰoHnéh₂m dh₃yéh₁t. sóh₂wl̥ séh₁mn̥ gʷʰr̥nuyéh₁t. gʷówes dukté.
english: Pull, cattle! Pull the plough! Bear the yoke! Make the furrow straight! Do not go astray! The heat burns, and we sweat. The man follows you. I sow the seed. May Mother Earth give grain! May the sun warm the seed! Pull, cattle!

pie: dyéw nos ph₂ter h₁uséwōm déh₃tor ḱludʰí. nu ḱós h₂éǵros h₂sowsós h₁ésti. dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr tr̥syéti. h₁yós méǵh₂m̥ h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰéns wódr̥ nos duh₃dʰí. h₁yós méǵh₂m̥ n̥bʰróm bʰéyds h₂éǵroy h₂ur̥sdʰí. gʰrómos gʷm̥yóyh₁t dʰoHnéh₂ pléh₁dʰoyh₁t. h₁wésu nos ǵr̥h₂nóm h₂uksyéh₁t bʰréh₁wr̥ pl̥h₁yéh₁t. h₁éḱwōs-kʷe káprōs píph₃oyh₁ent. h₂éboles h₁rudʰéh₁ih₁n̥t.
english: Father Sky, giver of good things, hear us! Now this field is dry. Mother Earth is thirsty. You who slew the great serpent, give us water! You who split the great rain-cloud, rain on the field! May thunder come, may the grain swell! May the good grain grow up for us, may the well become full! May the horses and the he-goats drink! May the apples be red!

pie: "tód h₁estu", wéwked lewkós deywós wérunos.
english: "Let this be so," said the bright god Werunos.

pie: gʰóstis kʷsépi h₁ért. pótis wérh₁t. gʰóstey h₁n̥dóm h₁idʰí. h₂Hséh₂i sddʰí. h₁ddʰí píph₃e-kʷe. gʰóstis démi lewbʰós h₁ésti. kʷís h₁ési? gʰóstis h₂éǵt. ǵʰwḗr h₂ówins h₁épt bʰéwgm̥-kʷe. pótis h₂éǵt. deywṓs toy h₁wésuh₂ dh₃ih₁ént.
english: A guest arrived in the night. The master said: "Guest, go inside! Sit down by the hearth! Eat and drink! A guest is dear in the house. Who are you?" The guest said: "A wild beast seized the sheep, and I fled." The master said: "May the gods give you good things!"

pie: súHnew h₂ówins ǵn̥nh₃dʰí. gʷṓs bʰréh₁wr̥ wédʰe. h₁yód h₂ówis leléykʷeti h₁íh₂m̥ h₂isḱé. tóns h₁régʷesi mē linékʷs. ḱwṓ h₁régʷesi tewóm h₃ókʷs h₁ésti. h₁yód ǵʰwḗr gʷémeti ḱunéy HrudHdʰí. mē tréses. h₁yós bʰéwdʰeti só swā́s h₂ówins péh₂sti.
english: Know the sheep, son! Lead the cattle to the well. If a sheep is missing, seek it. Do not leave them in the darkness. The dog is your eye in the darkness. If a wild beast arrives, cry out to the dog. Do not tremble. He who is awake guards his own sheep.

pie: h₁regʷesyét. h₂óweyes l̥gʰté. gʷówes l̥gʰté. spéḱs bʰéwdʰeti. péh₂wr̥ h₁rudʰéh₁ti. supnós wos h₁pyéh₁t. ǵʰwḗr mē gʷm̥sḱóyh₁t. h₁éy h₁íh₂n̥s mē widóyh₁t. h₂wéseti.
english: It was getting dark. Lie down, sheep! Lie down, cattle! The watcher is awake. The fire is red. May Sleep seize you! May the wild beast not arrive! May it not see them! It will become bright.

pie: nu h₃réḱs pótnih₂ súHnum ǵeǵonh₁e.
english: The king's lady bore a son.

pie: h₂éḱōs skinédomes. bʰórom wéǵʰōmes. wérǵom pl̥h₁éwbʰis ǵʰóstōys HéHḱu h₁ésti. gʷʰrensós dʰégʷʰeti puHrós-kʷe h₂sowsós h₁ésti. h₂éboles h₁rowdʰṓs h₁sénti. h₂éboln̥s-kʷe wósh₂r̥ h₂éḱh₃omes. h₁erkʷóm bʰéh₂omes. léwbʰe médʰu píph₃e. swésor ǵr̥h₂nóm gʷr̥h₃é. méwdomes.
english: Let us cut the ears of grain! Let us transport the load! With many hands the work is swift. The heat burns, and the wheat is dry. The apples are red. Let us eat up the apples and the garlic! Let us speak a hymn of praise! Drink mead, dear one! Eat grain, sister! Let us be joyful!

pie: dʰéǵʰom ǵénh₁mn̥ tewṓys h₂r̥Hmṓys ḱéle. nu toy séh₁mn̥ séh₁yomes. dʰoHnéh₂m nos dh₃dʰí puHróm nos h₁opéye. h₁íd nos h₂uksyéh₁t h₁íd mē mr̥yéh₁t. wréh₂des sth₂réh₂es h₁sih₁ént wósh₂r̥ pléh₁dʰoyh₁t. puHrósyo h₂éḱōs polh₁úh₂ h₁syéh₁t. wósh₂r̥ bʰuHyóyh₁t h₃ósdos wr̥h₂dés bʰuHyóyh₁t.
english: Earth, cover the seed in your arms! Now we sow the seed for you. Give us grain, give us wheat! May it grow up for us, may it not die! May the roots be firm, may the garlic swell! May the ears of wheat be many! May the garlic grow, may the branch grow from the root!

pie: kʷís ph₂ter h₂éǵrom h₂élomes? wódr̥ h₁ím h₂életi. kʷís wódr̥ h₂életi? dyḗws h₁íd h₂életi. kʷís dyḗm h₂életi? ne kʷis h₁ésti. h₁éy nos ph₂tḗr h₁ésti.
english: "Father, who nourishes the field?" "Water nourishes it." "Who nourishes the water?" "Sky nourishes it." "Who nourishes Sky?" "There is no one. He is a father to us."

pie: piḱtéh₂ gʷḗn h₂éHsh₂m̥ h₁r̥sḱét. h₁íh₂ h₁íh₂m̥ péri h₁éyt. h₁ésyeh₂s méh₂tēr HréwdHt h₂éǵt-kʷe. dʰúgh₂ter póteyey lewbʰṓy bʰúHdʰi. h₁ésyeh₂s bʰréh₂tēr h₁ésyeh₂ey h₂éh₂usosyo dóh₃r̥ h₁áyt. pótis h₁ésyeh₂ey mélit h₁áyt. h₁íh₂ h₁íd h₂éḱh₃t. nu h₁éy wérh₁t. gʷénh₂ ḱósyo déms pótnih₂ bʰúHdʰi. tewṓs suHnúes polh₁éwes h₁sih₁ént. h₂éHsh₂ sth₂réh₂ h₁syéh₁t.
english: The adorned woman came to the hearth. She went around it. Her mother cried and said: "Daughter, become dear to the husband!" Her brother gave her a gift of gold. The husband gave her honey. She ate it. Then he said: "Woman, become the mistress of this house! May your sons be many! May the hearth stand firm!"

pie: deywṓs gʷṓs-kʷe h₂ówins h₂léksete. káprons-kʷe h₁éḱwons h₂léksete. gʷíh₃woyh₁ent polh₁ús-kʷe h₁sih₁ént. h₂ŕ̥tḱos tóns kʷsépi mē h₁pyéh₁t. spéḱs bʰéwdʰoyh₁t moysós-kʷe kápros gʷíh₃woyh₁ent. h₂éwsosm̥-ge widóyh₁ent.
english: Gods, guard the cattle and the sheep! Guard the he-goats and the horses! May they live and be many. May the bear not seize them in the night. May the watcher be awake, may the ram and the he-goat live. May they indeed see Dawn!

pie: póteys suHnús h₂ówins h₂éǵrom h₂éǵet. HréwdHt. ǵʰwḗr gʷegʷóme. wiHrṓs h₂én h₁ludʰónt. ne kʷid kʷḱént. méwdt. h₁íns trís dʰréwgʰt. ǵʰwḗr-ge gʷémt. HréwdHt h₁ím-kʷe kʷis ne ḱléwt. h₁éy h₁íh₂n̥s h₁épt. h₁yós dʰrugʰyéti h₁ím kʷis ne ḱléwseti.
english: A master's son drove the sheep to the pasture. He cried: "A wild beast has come!" The men arrived there. They caught sight of nothing. He became joyful. Thrice he deceived them. A wild beast indeed came. He cried, and no one heard him. It seized them. Whoever deceives, no one listens to him.

pie: h₂éwsos píḱteh₂ diwés dʰúgh₂ter lukdʰí. h₁yéh₂ méǵh₂ h₁régʷos h₂epó ǵʰéys. gʷṓs h₂éǵrom gʷowsth₂ṓd h₁éǵʰs wédʰe. gʷíh₃woyh₁ent polh₁ús-kʷe h₁sih₁ént. widóyh₁ent te sóh₂wl̥ te sékʷetor.
english: Dawn, adorned daughter of Sky, shine! You who drive away the great darkness! Lead the cattle out of the cow-stall to the pasture. May they live and be many. May they see you, behind you the sun follows.

pie: h₁regʷesyét. h₂nḗr-kʷe gʷḗn l̥gʰtā́m. supnós tóh₁ lémbʰt. péh₂wr̥ h₁rudʰéh₁t. ḱwṓ h₂Hséh₂i légʰyet bʰéwdʰet-kʷe tóh₁-kʷe h₂lékset. h₂éwis HréwdHt. léwkt. stéh₂t.
english: It was getting dark. The man and the woman lay down. Sleep seized them. The fire was red. The dog lay at the hearth, and was awake, and guarded them. A bird cried. It became bright. He stood up.

pie: h₁regʷesyét. gʰrómos gʷm̥yét. nu n̥bʰrós upér stéh₂t. h₂élbʰit trémt. wiHrós h₂éǵroy sth₂éh₁yet. tr̥mónts h₁éy HréwdHt. ń̥bʰre h₂éḱōs mē Hrunéps. h₂epó gʷh₂dʰí. h₁éy h₁ím ḱléwt. h₁éy h₂epó gʷéh₂t h₁íh₂-kʷe ne Hrunépt. léwkt. n̥th₂grṓs h₁sént. h₁éy dʰémbʰt méwdt-kʷe.
english: It was getting dark. Thunder came. Then a rain-cloud rose above. The barley trembled. The man was standing in the field. Trembling, he cried: "Rain-cloud, do not break the ears of grain! Go away!" It heard him. It went away, and it did not break the ears of grain. It became bright. They were untouched. He was astonished, and became joyful.

pie: tréyes lewbʰṓs gʰósteyes gʷm̥yónt. pótis tóns h₂Hséh₂i sodéyet. h₁ésyo pótnih₂ puHróm-kʷe wósh₂r̥ pékʷet tóns-kʷe bʰoréyet. tóns h₂ḱh₃ént médʰu-kʷe trís píph₃ont. tetr̥pḗr. h₂éǵt. dyḗws ph₂tḗr ḱóm dṓm h₂léksoyh₁t.
english: Three dear guests came. The master seated them by the hearth. His wife cooked the wheat and the garlic and carried them around. They ate them up and drank mead thrice. They were satisfied. He said: "May Father Sky guard this house!"

pie: dʰéǵʰom toy puHróm-kʷe h₂élbʰit dédh₃mes. mélit-kʷe ǵʰutóm médʰu h₁opéyomes. h₁rowdʰóns toy h₂éboln̥s h₁opéyomes. tewóm dóh₃r̥ méǵh₂ h₁ésti. dóh₃r̥ h₁áyso gʷérHtores h₁smés. ǵénh₁mn̥ nos wésni h₁opéye. méǵh₂s-ge-kʷe h₁wésus h₁syéh₁s.
english: Earth, we give you wheat and barley. We give honey and the poured mead, we give you red apples. Great is your gift. Receive the gift, we are praisers. Give us seed in spring. May you indeed be great and good!

pie: ǵʰéslom gʷówes-kʷe ḱm̥tóm h₁éḱwōs h₃rēǵéy h₁sént dwóh₁ gʷówh₁ poh₂imnéy h₁stā́m. tr̥nóm ǵʰéymn̥ gʷémt. ǵʰéslom h₃rēǵés gʷówes h₂éǵroy m̥rént. poh₂imḗn dwóh₁ swóh₁ gʷówh₁ dṓm wédʰet gʷíh₃wom-kʷe. h₃rḗǵs tóm dṓm wésni gʷm̥sḱét. poh₂imḗn h₁ésmey médʰu déh₃t. h₃rḗǵs h₁íd péh₃t méwdt-kʷe. h₁éy h₁ésmey ḱm̥tóm h₂ówins h₁áyt.
english: The king had a thousand cattle and a hundred horses, the shepherd had two cattle. A sharp winter arrived. The king's thousand cattle died in the field. The shepherd led his own two cattle into the house, and they lived. In spring the king came to that house. The shepherd gave him mead. The king drank it and became joyful. He gave him a hundred sheep.

pie: ǵʰéyōm wésni tinéh₁ti h₂nḗr-kʷe h₂érh₃trōy gʷṓs yéwgt. h₁íns wédʰonts h₁éy h₂éǵrom h₂éryeti. sth₂róm h₂érh₃trom swṓys ǵʰóstōys kapyéti swidyéti-kʷe. h₂éweyes h₂érh₃trom sékʷontor. h₁erkʷóm bʰéh₂ti. nu h₁ésyo pótnih₂ séh₁mn̥ séh₁yeti lóyseh₂-kʷe h₁íd ḱéleti. h₂wérst. h₁yód sóh₂wl̥-kʷe n̥bʰrós gʷm̥tā́m ǵr̥h₂nóm h₂wékst h₁ésyo-kʷe ḱḗr méwdt.
english: In spring the snow melts, and the man yokes the cattle to the plough. Leading them, he ploughs the field. He holds the firm plough with his own hands, and sweats. Birds follow the plough. He speaks a hymn of praise. Then his wife sows the seed, and the furrow covers it. It rains. When the sun and the rain arrive, the grain grows up, and his heart becomes joyful.

pie: bʰréh₂ter h₂ówins kúdʰe h₂éǵesi? h₁íh₂n̥s bʰréh₁wr̥ h₂éǵoh₂. h₂éǵros h₂sowsós h₁ésti. ǵʰwḗrm̥ dedórḱth₂e? h₁ím kʷis ne dedórḱe. ḱwṓ h₁ím kʷsépi ḱléwt. kúdʰe tḱéysi? sélesi h₁épi tḱéymi. kʷíd bʰéresi? h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m bʰéroh₂. bʰréh₂ter gʷíh₃we. deywṓs h₁íh₂n̥s h₂léksoyh₁ent.
english: "Where are you driving the sheep, brother?" "I am driving them to the well. The field is dry." "Have you seen the wild beast?" "No one has seen him. The dog heard him in the night." "Where do you dwell?" "I dwell near the marsh." "What are you carrying?" "I am carrying wool." "Live, brother! May the gods guard them!"

pie: sh₂wéns kʷékʷle h₂éǵrom gʷʰr̥nudʰí. polh₁úh₂ puHrósyo h₂éḱōs pékʷe. kʷékʷle h₂élbʰitih₁ mē h₁éwsoyh₁s. kʷékʷle méǵh₂s h₁ési h₁ím spéḱye. puHrṓy gʷʰrensóm h₁opéye. ń̥dʰgʷʰitom nos ḱléwos h₁opéye.
english: Wheel of the sun, warm the field! Ripen the many ears of wheat! Wheel, may you not burn the barley! Wheel, you are great, look upon it. Give heat to the wheat. Give us imperishable fame.

pie: h₁regʷesyét. h₂óweyes gʰórtoy légʰyont. nu wĺ̥kʷos h₁régʷesos h₁ludʰét. nu h₁éy h₁íh₂n̥s sérpet. tr̥mént. moysós h₂énti stéh₂t. h₁ésyo h₃ókʷih₁ h₁rowdʰóy h₁stā́m. wĺ̥kʷos h₁ím h₁épt. nu ḱwṓ gʷm̥yét. wĺ̥kʷos h₁ím léh₁t bʰéwgt-kʷe. moysósyo h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ kruh₂séh₁ h₁rowdʰéh₂ h₁ést. moysós gʷíh₃wet.
english: It was getting dark. The sheep lay in the enclosure. Then a wolf arrived out of the darkness. Then it crept toward them. They trembled. The ram stood up in front. Its eyes were red. The wolf seized him. Then the dog came. The wolf let him go, and fled. The ram's wool was red with blood. The ram lived.

pie: awis akwabʰyams ā wawakat: kard agʰnutai mai widanti manum akwams agantam.
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: pótis suHnówey wérh₁t. gʷṓs toy dédeh₃mi. h₂éǵrons toy dédeh₃mi. h₁ím h₂érye tóns ph₂sdʰí. tewóm bʰréh₂term̥ mē dʰrugʰyés. mē stéh₂yes. h₁ésyo térmn̥ sth₂róm h₁ésti. bʰoydʰéh₂m memn̥dʰí. h₁wésu toy ḱléwos h₁syéh₁t.
english: The master said to the son: "I give you the cattle. I give you the field. Plough it, guard them. Do not deceive your brother. Do not steal. Its boundary is firm. Remember the pledge. May good fame be yours!"
